title: Walmart Has Raised Its Dividend 53 Straight Years. I'd Buy It Before December and Never Sell.
detail:
Walmart Has Raised Its Dividend 53 Straight Years. I'd Buy It Before December and Never Sell.
Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 12:05 PM MST 5 min read
WMT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) had a good morning on Thursday, Nov. 19. Sales and profit topped Wall Street's estimates, and the company raised its full-year forecast. Then the stock fell about 2% in early trading anyway.

I've learned to love earnings days like this. A dip on good news is often the cheapest way into a company that has raised its dividend for 53 straight years. This move of 50 consecutive dividend raises places Walmart in the coveted Dividend King category. These are companies that have raised their payouts for 50 years or more.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

A quarter that explains the streak

CEO John Furner summed up the quarter in one line: "The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more."

What he means is that Walmart's stores are no longer just places you walk into to make a purchase. They have become launchpads for online orders, and more than a third of the orders filled from stores reached shoppers in under three hours. That speed is winning new kinds of customers, too, as Walmart said its share gains were led by upper-income households.

CFO John David Rainey said the quarter also brought Walmart's biggest market share gains in food in three years. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses," he told CNBC.

The part I find most exciting doesn't involve a shopping cart at all. Walmart's U.S. advertising business grew 37%, its membership fee revenue rose 17% worldwide, and sales on its online marketplace, where outside sellers pay to reach Walmart's shoppers, jumped 49%.

Brands pay to show up where millions of people shop, and members pay a yearly fee whether they buy a TV or a gallon of milk. That's how Walmart can keep cutting prices and still grow profit, and it's what makes the dividend feel so durable to me.

Image source: Getty Images.

Then there's Sparky, Walmart's AI shopping assistant. Its U.S. usage has more than doubled from a year ago, and Furner said shoppers who use it build baskets about 40% bigger on average. Shopping may increasingly start with a question typed into an app instead of a walk down an aisle, and Walmart wants to be the one answering it.

The newest piece is a $120-a-year bundle of Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus. Furner told CNBC it has brought about 2 million new people into Sam's Club since it launched in late October, and Rainey said bundle members are "spending appreciably more." There's a catch, though: Walmart expects the bundle to weigh on Sam's Club profit growth until late 2027.

Investors choosing between growth and stability often weigh the explosive potential of cosmetics against the steady demand for energy drinks. This comparison evaluates whether e.l.f. Beauty (NYSE:ELF) or Monster Beverage (NASDAQ:MNST) is the better buy.

e.l.f. Beauty disrupts the traditional makeup industry by offering high-speed product innovation and prestige-quality items at accessible prices. Monster Beverage dominates the beverage coolers with its diverse energy portfolio and global scale. Both companies have delivered impressive long-term results, but they offer distinct risk and reward profiles for retail investors.

The case for e.l.f. Beauty

e.l.f. Beauty operates in the competitive segment of consumer staples stocks, focusing on high-quality cosmetics at accessible price points. The company sells its products through mass, drug, and specialty retail channels, including key partners like Target (NYSE:TGT), Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). These retail relationships account for nearly 76% of net sales, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.9 billion. This represented revenue growth of roughly 39.9% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for those 12 months was approximately $86.6 million, supported by a net margin of close to 4.5%.

As of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.8x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a company funds its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 2.3x. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $190.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 40.9% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Monster Beverage

Monster Beverage functions as a holding company for major energy brands like Reign, NOS, and Bang. It primarily distributes its beverages through an extensive network of bottlers, relying on Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) as its primary global distribution partner. The company currently serves a growing number of international markets across 80 countries, leveraging this massive network to maintain its market lead.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $9.6 billion. This reflects revenue growth of approximately 20.2% over the previous year. Net income for the period was nearly $2.2 billion, resulting in a healthy net margin of approximately 22.7%.

title: Walmart makes tough decision that may upset shoppers
detail:
Walmart makes tough decision that may upset shoppers
Maurie Backman, Celine Provini
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 8:07 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For many consumers, Walmart is one of the most reliable places to turn when they need something at the last minute. 

Whether it's groceries for dinner, an extra household essential, or a forgotten ingredient for a holiday meal, shoppers have grown accustomed to being able to stop by the retailer throughout much of the year.

But there are two days when that convenience comes to a complete stop.

Walmart will close all of its U.S. stores on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, and Christmas Day, Dec. 25, 2026. 

And that decision could frustrate shoppers who depend on the retailer for last-minute purchases, particularly as families prepare for one of the busiest holiday periods of the year.

Walmart is closing stores on 2 major holidays

Walmart has confirmed that its U.S. stores will close on Thanksgiving and Christmas this year.

However, stores will operate regular hours on Wednesday, Nov. 25, before closing for Thanksgiving the following day, according to the company's official 2026 holiday schedule.

The good news is that Walmart locations are scheduled to reopen at 6 a.m. for Black Friday. 

The retailer will also adjust its hours on Christmas Eve. Stores will close at 6 p.m. on Dec. 24 before remaining closed throughout Christmas Day.

Unlike some retailers that close on several holidays throughout the year, Walmart limits its annual full-store closures to these two occasions. Costco, for example, has seven closures.

Of course, Thanksgiving in particular can create a challenge for shoppers who realize they're missing an ingredient or need additional supplies shortly before guests arrive.

However, Walmart is encouraging customers to plan ahead and take advantage of its shopping and delivery options throughout the holiday season.

The company has also been expanding its convenience offerings, including Express Pickup, which allows customers to have eligible orders ready in as little as one hour. Those services could help shoppers avoid some of the stress associated with holiday preparations.

Walmart will be closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.Image source: Walmart
Walmart prioritizes employees during the holidays

There's a business argument for Walmart to remain open on Thanksgiving and Christmas. With millions of customers shopping throughout the holiday season, the retailer could potentially capture loads of additional sales by operating on those days.

But Walmart has repeatedly indicated that giving employees time with their families is more important.

title: PepsiCo vs. Starbucks: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
PepsiCo vs. Starbucks: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Erin Kennedy, The Motley Fool

PEP
SBUX
WMT

Trading disclosure

Investors choosing between PepsiCo (NASDAQ:PEP) and Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX) must weigh steady snack-and-sip diversification against premium coffee growth. Both brands dominate their niches, but different economic tailwinds will likely determine the winner in 2027.

PepsiCo uses a massive snack and drink catalog to capture reliable shelf space globally. Starbucks focuses on premium retail experiences and beverage innovation in 88 markets. Comparing their cash flow and valuation metrics helps determine which giant offers more value over the next few years.

The case for PepsiCo

PepsiCo sells a variety of snacks and beverages to wholesale distributors, retail chains, and foodservice operators. Its largest customer is Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), which accounted for approximately 14% of revenue in 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, though long-term deals with partners like Yum! Brands (NYSE:YUM) provide a stable foundation.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 5, 2026, revenue reached nearly $98.2 billion, an increase of roughly 6.4%. Net income reached approximately $10.9 billion. This performance suggests a steady trajectory for its diversified portfolio of beverage and snack categories.

As of Pepsi's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio, which measures total debt against the value of assets owned by shareholders, was nearly 2.4. The current ratio reached approximately 0.9. This metric indicates the company's ability to cover its short-term debt with assets like cash and inventory. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, free cash flow was close to $7.7 billion, representing the cash remaining after covering all operating and capital investments.

The case for Starbucks

Starbucks operates thousands of coffeehouses and sells packaged coffee through a global alliance with Nestlé (OTC:NSRGF). The business depends on a loyal customer base for its company-operated stores and regional licensed partners. This model prioritizes the coffeehouse experience for millions of daily visitors while expanding through partnerships in ready-to-drink beverages.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached nearly $37.9 billion, representing growth of roughly 1.9%. Net income was approximately $2.5 billion. While revenue growth was modest, the company managed to maintain a net margin of close to 6.7% as it navigated shifting consumer habits.

As of Starbucks' September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly -2.9, which means total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. Its current ratio was close to 0.8. In the fiscal year ended Sept. 27, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $3.7 billion.

title: TD Cowen Raises Its Walmart Target to $147. Is It Still Too Low?

TD Cowen Raises Its Walmart Target to $147. Is It Still Too Low? ©Syda Productions and yangwenshuang from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

TD Cowen raised its Walmart price target to $147 from $125 and kept its Buy rating after a beat-and-raise quarter.

The firm expects fast e-commerce growth to lift margins, and at least eight other firms raised targets the same day.

Walmart trades at about 43x forward earnings, against 17x for Target and 48x for Costco, and $147 needs that premium to hold for another year.

$147 looks like Walmart's bull case, and the new mid-$130s targets look like the likelier landing.

Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) rose 1.5% to $127.95 on Friday, Nov. 20, while the Nasdaq fell 5.3%, a day after it beat its own guidance and raised its outlook again. TD Cowen lifted its price target to $147 from $125, 15% above Friday's close, and kept a Buy rating.

Target (TGT:NYSE) posted 5.6% comparable sales growth in its own third quarter, and Walmart's new $120 bundle of Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus goes after the warehouse shopper Costco (COST:NASDAQ) counts on.

A Beat, a Raise and a New Bundle

In the quarter to Oct. 31, adjusted EPS came in at $0.65, above Walmart's $0.62 to $0.64 guide, and adjusted operating income grew 5.5% in constant currency against a 2% to 4% guide. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance went to $2.84-$2.89 from $2.80-$2.87, its second raise this year.

Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% excluding fuel, and Sam's Club's rose 4.9%. CEO John Furner said Sam's has seen "a couple million new members come in and shop" since the bundle launched.

TD Cowen Is Betting on Walmart's E-Commerce Margins

TD Cowen's Max Rakhlenko said Walmart's e-commerce kept accelerating with stronger incremental margins, and he expects more "outsized" growth to lift margins. CFO John David Rainey put U.S. e-commerce incremental margins at over 12% in the quarter.

The new target takes TD Cowen most of the way back to the $150 it had before it cut to $125 after the stock fell on Walmart's August report. At least eight other firms, including Morgan Stanley, BofA and Jefferies, also raised targets on Friday, to between $135 and $145. The $132 consensus target, 3% above the price and set before the report, is still below its June peak of $139.

WMT Stock Mean Price Target: 1-Year (TIKR)
Does $147 Add Up?

Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from $2.64 last year to $3.62 in the year ending January 2029.

WMT Normalized EPS, Actual and Estimates: Years Ending January 2024-2028 (TIKR)

By my math, $147 is about 41x those earnings, a touch below today's 43x forward multiple. So the target doesn't need a higher multiple. At today's multiple, it needs next-12-month EPS of about $3.44 a year from now, up 15% from today's $3.00.

WMT Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

At its five-year average of 29.7x, $3.62 is worth about $107 a share. Walmart already costs more than twice Target's 17x forward earnings and sits near Costco's 48x (both as of Nov. 19).

title: Walmart's CEO shares big news for time-strapped grocery shoppers
detail:
Walmart's CEO shares big news for time-strapped grocery shoppers
Mwangi Enos, Celine Provini
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 7:37 PM MST 5 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Picture a random Tuesday at 5 p.m. You're tired, the fridge is half empty, and four people are about to ask what's for dinner.

I'm certain most of you have lived that moment, and most have lost about 40 minutes to it.

Walmart (WMT) CEO John Furner says the company aims to be there for customers in moments like these, and that is precisely the problem it is trying to solve. He knows it personally.

He and his wife raised four kids, all now in college, and he described a family that is "really busy."

The adoption is encouraging, and agentic shopping is definitely part of what we're doing.

"It's not the only thing we do, of course, but it's part of the solution," Furner told CNBC's "Squawk Box" from Walmart's headquarters in Bentonville, Arkansas.

Also Read: What happens after Walmart leaves town is worse than expected

How Walmart's Sparky AI assistant turns dinner planning into one tap

Sparky is Walmart's conversational shopping assistant. It launched in June 2025 and works in English, Spanish, and French across the U.S., Mexico, and Canada. In the U.S. app, you tap the smiley face at the bottom of the screen.

Furner described how his household uses it. You type something like "dinner tonight at 5:00 for four people," or you enter a full week of meals. Sparky suggests recipes with pictures, prep time, cook time, and price per person. It also flags ingredients you probably already own, based on recent purchases.

"With one click, 30 or 40 minutes later, the whole thing can be there," Furner said. "It's just an easy way for busy families and busy individuals to save time."

Is anyone using it? Based on results released Nov. 19, U.S. usage of Sparky rose 129% year over year (YoY) in the third quarter. The baskets of shoppers who used it were 40% larger.

Why the $120 membership bundle targets subscription fatigue

The bigger announcement for everyday households may be the membership. Walmart now offers Sam's Club Plus and Walmart Plus together for $120 annually, according to Walmart.

Furner pitched it with simple math. Buy the pieces separately, including delivery, the warehouse club, the marketplace, and streaming, and a customer could spend up to $400 a year, he said. Bundled, it comes to about $10 a month.

"What we're trying to build is the most essential membership in the United States," Furner said.

title: Walmart shares delivery update consumers need to know about

Walmart shares delivery update consumers need to know about
Maurie Backman
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 10:17 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart has become an increasingly important destination for consumers looking to save money on groceries and everyday essentials. 

But low prices aren't the only reason shoppers keep returning to the retailer. Convenience is becoming just as important.

As more consumers turn to online shopping, Walmart is making significant investments in its delivery network, using its thousands of physical stores to get products into customers' hands faster.

The strategy is already producing results, and the company recently shared an update that could have major implications for how Americans shop.

Walmart expands delivery reach using its stores

During the company's third quarter 2027 earnings call, Walmart CEO John Furner discussed how the retailer's expanding delivery capabilities are helping connect its stores and digital operations.

"We no longer see stores and e-commerce as separate, but connected parts of an integrated ecosystem," Furner told analysts.

Furner also said, "We can now reach 96% of U.S. households in less than three hours, and 60% in less than 30 minutes. We have a unique ability to get closer to customers, use inventory more effectively, and deliver with speed at a low relative cost."

The comments highlight an important shift in Walmart's business model. 

Rather than treating online shopping and traditional store visits as competing channels, the retailer is increasingly using them together to improve convenience and attract more customers.

For shoppers, that could mean faster deliveries, more available products, and fewer reasons to shop elsewhere.

The company is also making more products available for local delivery by placing select marketplace inventory in stores. That means customers can access a broader assortment without necessarily waiting for products to arrive from distant fulfillment centers.

Walmart is also expanding beyond traditional retail orders. Furner said the company is using its delivery capabilities to support quick-service restaurant partners, allowing customers to order food alongside other essentials.

Iv-olga/Shutterstock.com
Walmart's loyal customers keep coming back

Walmart's delivery expansion also comes as the retailer benefits from consistent customer traffic.

A Placer.ai report examined foot traffic and shopping frequency at Walmart and Target during the third quarter of 2026. It found that Walmart's overall visits increased 0.7% year over year, while same-store visits rose 0.6%.

Perhaps more importantly, 67.7% of Walmart visitors came to the retailer at least twice during an average month, suggesting Walmart has maintained a remarkably consistent base of repeat shoppers.
